title: Who sets the deadline?
hook: Would you choose one final deadline or several costly checkpoints?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare self-imposed deadlines with externally spaced deadlines without claiming a universal best schedule.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare self-imposed deadlines with externally spaced deadlines without claiming a universal best schedule.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy schedule allocates two hours on each of three days, with capacity three hours per day. How many scheduled hours exceed a day’s capacity? Toy inputs A=[2, 2, 2, 3]; B=[0, 0, 6, 3].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[6, 2, 0], [6, 6, 3]]. Labels: Total hours, Peak hours, Overload hours.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Both schedules contain the same work, but their daily peaks differ. Spacing can satisfy this model’s capacity constraint while a single deadline overloads one day. That is a scheduling calculation, not a universal finding about imposed deadlines.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Day 1 hours=0, Day 2 hours=0, Day 3 hours=6, Daily capacity=3. What is Overload hours? Answer: 3.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Day 1 hours=0, Day 2 hours=0, Day 3 hours=6, Daily capacity=3. What is Overload hours?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 3. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Students set themselves costly deadlines, but evenly spaced imposed deadlines produced the best work (Ariely & Wertenbroch, 2002).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Compare self-imposed deadlines with externally spaced deadlines without claiming a universal best schedule.
